messages:
anya: Starting an experiment to tweak fair-share batch splitting for conversational routes. Goal: get p95 under 120ms without regressing error rate or cost. Will test split + token budget by tier.

omar: what's the current token-budget / split baseline?

anya: prod baseline: chat route token_budget=512, completion=1024, batch_window_ms=8, fair_share_split=0.7. We see p95 ~135ms on busy hosts. Plan: reduce chat budget to 200 and split batches 65/35 (short/long) + bump window to 10–12ms in canary. config below.

kevin: watch out for KV cache churn when you change token budgets — smaller budgets can increase cache misses for multi-turn. Also kernel switch overhead shows up for microbatch size variance.

lisa: confirmed on profiling last week: kernel-handoff cost ~3.5–5ms if microbatch size oscillates; that eats into p95 gains. Need to tune queue-policy hysteresis.

anya: agreed. Canary plan: pin kernel affinity to f16 where available, enable fair-split, hysteresis=2000ms. Deploy to edge-canary-3 (5%).

anya: config (canary):
```json
{
  "batch_window_ms": 12,
  "fair_share_split": 0.65,
  "token_budget_by_route": {"chat": 200, "completion": 900},
  "queue_hysteresis_ms": 2000,
  "kernel_affinity": "prefer-f16"
}
```

ci-bot: deployed canary config to cluster/edge-canary-3 (5% traffic). :rocket:

perf-bot: canary snapshot (10m after rollout): chat p95 -9.2%, median +0.9%, kv_hit_rate -2.4%, tail L2-spills increased from 0.02% -> 0.08%. Error rate steady +0.03%.

omar: do we have trace ids for the L2-spills? want to see queue timing + kernel handoff.

anya: sample trace 0xdeadbeef: shows an early queueing spike then kernel affinity fallback -> kernel switch log lines. excerpt:
```
[trace 0xdeadbeef] queue_wait_ms=18 -> microbatch formed size=3 -> kernel_switch to f32 cost=4.2ms -> kv_miss spike (prefix=3) -> emit tokens
```

kevin: that matches expectation. Two quick levers: 1) raise batch_window to 14ms (more stable microbatch sizes) or 2) keep 12ms but increase fair_share_split toward longs for routes that hit kernel-switch frequently. Also consider relaxing token_budget for enterprise tier to avoid cache churn.

lisa: +1 on hysteresis; if queue-policy flips every 20–30s we create oscillation and kernel churn. Add a rolling-average over 10s for decisioning.

anya: updated proposal before next canary:
```json
{
  "batch_window_ms": 14,
  "fair_share_split": 0.6,
  "token_budget_by_tier": {"enterprise": 400, "paid": 300, "free": 120},
  "queue_hysteresis_ms": 5000,
  "decision_window_s": 10
}
```

perf-bot: scheduled next canary at 1748421800 (rolling 5% -> 20% if stable). Will capture p95, kv_hit, kernel_switch_count, error_rate.

omar: what's the rollback criteria?

anya: rollback if chat p95 > baseline OR error rate +0.5% absolute OR kernel_switch_count increases >20% without p95 improvement. Also cost threshold: >4% token-per-request increase.

kevin: one more note — be mindful of cross-route fairness: pushing chat down too hard can push latency to completion route if they share kernel pools. We may need route-aware pool separation for full gains.

lisa: logging/observability checklist: add tags for fair_split_version, batch_window_ms, decision_window_s to spans, and emit kv_hit_rate by prefix-length.

anya: thanks all — will run the next canary and post the diff. tagging @kevin for kernel-affinity follow-up. :white_check_mark:
